transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what really pushed me to make this appointment is that I'm having a lot of trouble finishing things at work. I keep starting follow-up items—like after audits or mentorship events—with every intention of finishing them. I sit down to do it, and then... I'll find out days later that the final email, or a review note, or some form never actually got done. It's happening a lot, and I just really need to figure out what's going on.
Did you have similar problems with attention or finishing tasks when you were a child?

Yes, actually. Even back in elementary school, my report cards always said the same kind of things. The teachers would write that I was bright, but I constantly lost my assignments or rushed through things and missed small details. I also talked out of turn a lot and always needed reminders to actually finish my work. My mother still jokes about it—she says I could ace a test with no problem, but completely forget to turn in the project that was sitting right there in my backpack. So, yeah, it's definitely been an issue for a long time.
Do these attention and follow-through problems cause difficulties for you outside of work too?

Yes, they definitely do. It's not just work, though work is getting bad. My mistakes and all those unfinished follow-ups actually affected a client review recently. I’m really worried people are starting to question if I can even handle the promotion I've been working toward. 

But at home... yeah, it's a problem there, too. My husband has basically had to take over paying the bills and handling commitments I agreed to do. He just... he can't count on me to actually get them done reliably. It's frustrating for both of us.
Do you often feel restless or have trouble staying seated when you’re expected to remain still?

Yes, I do. Sitting still for a long time, like during a lengthy client review, actually feels physically uncomfortable for me. It's almost like this pressure just keeps building up inside me until I feel like I absolutely have to stand up. I'll usually end up getting up to walk to the printer, or I'll just invent some other reason to move around because I can't just sit there anymore.
Do you often make careless mistakes because you miss small details?

Yes, unfortunately I do. It's actually really embarrassing for me because... well, detail is supposed to be my strength in my line of work. But even in reports where I know better than to rush, I'll still mess up. I'll miss a changed date, or I'll transpose a number... sometimes I even leave a placeholder comment right in the workpaper by accident. It just completely slips past me.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to solve?

No, not really. I mean, I stress about the mistakes I make at work or the things I forget to do at home, because those are actual problems happening right now. But I don't just sit around worrying about random things or things that haven't happened. My mind is usually just jumping from one thing to the next, not really stuck on worrying.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on a task or conversation, even when you’re trying to pay attention?

Yes, definitely. I can start a long client meeting, or maybe one of those AI-tool trainings we do at work, and I'll be fully engaged at the beginning. But after a while, my mind just... slips off. I'll suddenly realize I've completely missed the last few minutes of what was said, even though I'm still looking right at the screen and actively trying to pay attention.
Do you often act or speak before thinking, and then regret it afterward?

Not really, no. I don't think I have a problem with blurting things out or acting impulsively like that. I'm actually pretty careful about what I say, especially around the office or with clients. I might lose focus, like I mentioned, but I usually think before I speak. So, no, I haven't really noticed that being an issue for me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes when I mess up at work or forget something important, but I don't feel depressed or down most days. I generally feel okay mood-wise, just... easily distracted and a bit scattered. But not depressed.
Do you often put off tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort, like long reports or detailed paperwork?

No, not really. I mean, my whole job as an accountant is basically detailed paperwork and long reports. I do them every day. I might get distracted while I'm working on them, like I said before, but I don't avoid starting them or put them off. It's just part of the job, so I just sit down and do it.
When you have a task that will take a lot of sustained mental effort, do you usually avoid it or put it off?

I think you might have just asked me that, actually. But yeah, like I mentioned a second ago, no, I don't avoid them. Since I'm an accountant, that's pretty much my whole job. I don't put off starting the work, I just dive in, even if I end up getting sidetracked while I'm actually doing it.
Outside of work and home, do these attention problems also happen in other settings, like social situations or appointments?

Not really, no. I haven't really noticed any major issues when I'm out with friends or at appointments. It mostly just seems to be a problem when I'm trying to focus at work or trying to get things done around the house. When I'm out doing other things, I seem to do okay.
Before you turned 12, were these attention and follow-through problems already causing noticeable trouble for you?

Yeah, they were. Even back in elementary school, my report cards always had those kinds of comments. The teachers would say I was bright, but that I lost assignments, rushed past small details, talked out of turn... and that I needed reminders to actually finish my work. My mother actually still jokes about it today. She says I could completely ace a test, but then forget to turn in the project that was sitting right there in my backpack.
